ex-202-1.title: Motion along a straight line
ex-202-1.question: A cat walks on a straight fence. It first walks forwards for 10 s and the average speed is 0.6 m s−1. Then it walks backwards for 20 s and the average speed is 0.45 m s−1. Find its total displacement.
ex-202-1.answer:
Take forward as positive.

Displacement in first 10 s =+0.6×10=6 m

Displacement in next 20 s =−0.45×20=−9 m

Total displacement =+6+(−9)=−3 m

The total displacement is 3 m (backwards).
ex-202-1.tips:
Always assign the positive direction at the beginning.

v=st⇒ s=vt

ex-202-2.title: Average acceleration of a lion
ex-202-2.question: A lion is chased by a group of buffalos. It accelerates from rest to 12 m s−1 in 3 s along a straight line. Find its average acceleration.
ex-202-2.answer:
Take the moving direction of the lion as positive.

a=v−ut=12−03=4 m s−2

Its average acceleration is 4 m s−2 along its moving direction.

ex-202-3.title: Analyzing an s–t graph
ex-202-3.question:
The s−t graph of a girl walking along a straight road is as shown.

(a) During which time periods is the girl walking in the positive direction?

(b) Find (i) the displacement of the girl and (ii) the distance travelled by the girl from t=5 s to t=40 s.

(c) Find the velocities of the girl at t=5 s and t=40 s.

(d) Find the average velocity of the girl from t=0 to t=50 s.
ex-202-3.answer:
(a) During 0–10 s and 50–55 s.

(b) (i) Displacement =2−4=−2 m

(ii) Distance travelled =(8−4)+(8−2)=10 m

(c) Apply velocity = slope of s−t graph.

At t=5 s, velocity =8−010−0=0.8 m s−1.

At t=40 s, velocity =(−4)−850−30=−0.6 m s−1.

(d) Average velocity =(−4)−050−0=−0.08 m s−1.
ex-202-3.tips:
A sketch of the girl’s motion from t=5 s to t=40 s:

Constant velocity from t=0 to t=10 s.

Constant velocity from t=30 s to t=50 s.

st=total displacementtotal time of travel

ex-202-4.title: Finding acceleration from v–t graph
ex-202-4.question:
An MTR train travels along a straight track from Mong Kok to Prince Edward. Its v−t graph is as shown.

(a) Describe the motion of the train.

(b) Find the acceleration of the train at t=10 s and 55 s.
ex-202-4.answer:
(a) During 0–20 s, it speeds up from rest with a constant acceleration.

During 20–50 s, it is in uniform motion.

During 50–60 s, it slows down to rest with a constant deceleration.

(b) Apply acceleration = slope of v−t graph.

At t=10 s, acceleration =14−020−0=0.7 m s−2.

At t=55 s, acceleration =0−1460−50=−1.4 m s−2.
ex-202-4.tips: State clearly if the acceleration is constant. We usually do not need to state the direction of motion if it remains unchanged.

ex-202-5.title: Trolley moving along an inclined plane
ex-202-5.question:
A trolley is given a sharp push up a smooth inclined plane from point X at time t=0 (Fig a). After reaching the highest point, it slides down the plane. It moves along a straight line during the whole journey and reaches point Y at t=5 s. Its v−t graph is a straight line (Fig b). Take the direction up the plane as positive.

(a) When does the trolley reach the highest point?

(b) Find the acceleration of the trolley at t=3 s.

(c) Find the distance between X and Y.

(d) Find the distance travelled by the trolley in the whole journey.
ex-202-5.answer:
(a) At t=3 s.

(b) Acceleration = slope of v−t graph =0−33−0=−1 m s−2.

(c) Displacement over the whole journey = total area under v−t graph

=3×32−(5−3)×22=2.5 m

Therefore, the distance between X and Y is 2.5 m.

(d) Distance travelled =3×32+(5−3)×22=6.5 m.
ex-202-5.tips:
When the trolley reaches the highest point, it changes its direction of motion. This happens when the v−t graph crosses the horizontal axis.

The displacement is equal to the difference between the distances travelled in the upward journey and in the downward journey.

ex-202-7.title: Braking a snowmobile
ex-202-7.question:
A snowmobile moves along a straight line. At a certain instant, it starts braking to decelerate uniformly. Its speed decreases from 25 m s−1 to 15 m s−1 after travelling 40 m.

(a) Find the acceleration of the snowmobile.

(b) How much time does the snowmobile take to decelerate from 15 m s−1 to rest?
ex-202-7.answer:
(a) Take forwards as positive.

u=+25 m s−1, v=+15 m s−1, s=+40 m, a=?

By v2=u2+2as, 152=252+2a×40, so a=−5 m s−2.

The acceleration of the snowmobile is 5 m s−2 (backwards).

(b) Consider the motion from 15 m s−1 to rest.

u=+15 m s−1, v=0, a=−5 m s−2, t=?

By v=u+at, 0=15+(−5)t, so t=3 s.

It takes 3 s to decelerate from 15 m s−1 to rest.
ex-202-7.tips:
Skill Problem solving Applying equations of motion

1. Define the positive direction.

2. Find out which variables are known, and which are to be found. The signs of the variables should be consistent with the positive direction. Remember to use proper units for the variables.

3. Choose the suitable equation. Each equation should have 3 known variables and only 1 unknown.

ex-202-8.title: Skid marks
ex-202-8.question: A police officer is investigating a car accident. The car stopped after leaving skid marks of 20 m. It is also found from CCTV that the braking lasted 1.7 s. What was the speed of the car just before it braked?
ex-202-8.answer:
Take forwards as positive.

s=+20 m, t=1.7 s, v=0, u=?

By s=(u+v)t2,

20=(u+0)×1.72

u=23.5 m s−1

The speed of the car was 23.5 m s−1 just before it braked.
ex-202-8.tips: This example shows how the skid marks can help the police to estimate the initial speed of the car as asked on p.62.

ex-202-9.title: Stopping distance
ex-202-9.question:
A car travels at 63 km h−1 along a straight road. The driver sees an obstacle 30 m ahead and starts braking the car after a reaction time of 0.8 s. The car slows down uniformly at 7 m s−2 during braking.

(a) Find the thinking distance, i.e. the distance travelled during the driver’s reaction time.

(b) Find the braking distance, i.e. the distance travelled during braking to a stop.

(c) Does the car hit the obstacle?
ex-202-9.answer:
(a) 63 km h−1=633.6 m s−1=17.5 m s−1

Thinking distance = speed × reaction time =17.5×0.8=14 m.

(b) Consider the motion during braking. Take forwards as positive.

u=+17.5 m s−1, v=0, a=−7 m s−2, s=?

By v2=u2+2as,

02=17.52+2(−7)× s

s=21.9 m

The braking distance is 21.9 m.

(c) Yes.
ex-202-9.tips:
Assume the car moves at a constant velocity during the reaction time.

The stopping distance, i.e. the total distance for the car to stop after the driver notices the obstacle, is equal to 35.9 m (= 14 + 21.9), which is longer than 30 m.

ex-202-11.title: Falling object
ex-202-11.question:
A piece of concrete falls from rest at a height 40 m above the ground from an old building. Neglect air resistance and take the acceleration due to gravity to be 9.81 m s−2.

(a) How long does the concrete take to reach the ground?

(b) What is the speed of the concrete when it reaches the ground?
ex-202-11.answer:
Method 1 Take upwards as positive

(a) u=0, s=−40 m, a=−9.81 m s−2, t=?

By s=ut+12at2, −40=0+12×(−9.81)× t2.

t=2.86 s or −2.86 s (rejected).

The concrete takes 2.86 s to reach the ground.

(b) u=0, s=−40 m, a=−9.81 m s−2, v=?

By v2=u2+2as, v2=02+2(−9.81)(−40).

v=28.0 m s−1 (rejected) or −28.0 m s−1.

The speed of the concrete is 28.0 m s−1 when it reaches the ground.

Method 2 Take downwards as positive

(a) u=0, s=+40 m, a=+9.81 m s−2, t=?

By s=ut+12at2, 40=0+12×9.81× t2.

t=2.86 s or −2.86 s (rejected).

The concrete takes 2.86 s to reach the ground.

(b) u=0, s=+40 m, a=+9.81 m s−2, v=?

By v2=u2+2as, v2=02+2×9.81×40.

v=28.0 m s−1 or −28.0 m s−1 (rejected).

The speed of the concrete is 28.0 m s−1 when it reaches the ground.
ex-202-11.tips:
The problem can be solved in two different ways.

Why is the answer t=−2.86 s rejected?

Use the values given in the question instead of those calculated from the previous part if possible to avoid error caused by rounding.

Why is the answer v=28.0 m s−1 rejected when taking upward as positive and the answer v=−28.0 m s−1 rejected when taking downward as positive?

From Example 11, we can see that no matter which direction is taken as positive, the same numerical answer with the correct direction can be obtained by using the equations of uniformly accelerated motion.

ex-202-12.title: Serving a tennis ball
ex-202-12.question:
At time t=0, Simon throws a tennis ball vertically upwards at 7 m s−1 from a height of 1.70 m above the ground. When the ball falls back to a height of 3.30 m, Simon hits it. Neglect air resistance and take g=9.81 m s−2.

(a) What is the maximum height above the ground reached by the ball?

(b) When does Simon hit the ball?
ex-202-12.answer:
Take upwards as positive.

(a) Consider the upward motion to the maximum height.

u=+7 m s−1, v=0, a=−9.81 m s−2, s=?

By v2=u2+2as, 02=72+2×(−9.81)× s.

s=2.50 m

Maximum height above the ground =1.70+2.50=4.20 m.

(b) Consider the motion from the starting position to the height 3.30 m via the maximum height.

u=+7 m s−1, a=−9.81 m s−2, s=+(3.30−1.70)=+1.60 m, t=?

By s=ut+12at2,

1.60=7t+12×(−9.81)× t2

4.905t2−7t+1.60=0


Using the quadratic formula with the coefficients from the preceding equation,

t=−(−7)±(−7)2−4(4.905)(1.60)2×4.905

t=1.14 s or 0.286 s (rejected).

Simon hits the ball at t=1.14 s.
ex-202-12.tips:
Skill Mathematics The quadratic formula

Textbook reference: p.454.

You may also solve this question by dividing the motion into two parts (upwards and downwards) and finding the time for completing each part of motion separately.

Source correction

The source prints the substitution line as

t=−(−7)±(−7)2−4(4.905)(1.10)2×1.10

This line contains printing errors. The constant term is 1.60 and the denominator is 2×4.905, as shown in the corrected equation above. The source’s final answers, 1.14 s and 0.286 s, agree with the corrected equation.
